mean: to drag up old grievances during an argument
lit: to leaf back through the old account books

use.how: Verb-object phrase, often after 别、又、老; can split (翻什么旧账, 翻起旧账来). Said of bringing up past wrongs in a quarrel, mostly between couples, family or friends.

near.diff: 揭短 exposes someone's faults or secrets, often in front of others; 翻旧账 brings up old wrongs that were supposed to be settled.

cue: In the middle of a row about the washing-up, your partner starts listing every mistake you made over the last five years. What are they doing?

ctx.s: 吵架归吵架，别老是{翻旧账}。
ctx.en: Argue if you must, but stop dragging up the past.

ctx.s: 我不过是忘了倒垃圾，她就{翻起旧账}来，从结婚那年说起。
ctx.en: I only forgot to take out the rubbish, and she started raking up old grievances, going right back to the year we married.

ctx.s: “上次你也迟到了！”“都过去半年了，你还{翻什么旧账}？”
ctx.en: "You were late last time too!" "That was six months ago, why are you bringing it up again?"

ctx.s: 今天开会是讨论下一步怎么办，不是来{翻旧账}的。
ctx.en: This meeting is about what to do next, not about raking over old grievances.

ctx.s: 两个人本来已经和好了，结果一喝酒又开始{翻旧账}。
ctx.en: The two of them had already made up, but as soon as they had a drink they started dredging up the past again.

ctx.s: 夫妻之间最伤感情的，就是吵架时{翻旧账}。
ctx.en: Nothing hurts a marriage more than dragging up old grievances in an argument.

bad.s: 周末我们一起{翻旧账}，看了很多小时候的照片。
bad.en: (meant: at the weekend we reminisced and looked at childhood photos)
bad.why: It means raking up old grievances in a quarrel, not fond reminiscing; for that say huiyi guoqu (recall the past).

bad.s: 他昨天又{翻旧账}我了。
bad.en: (meant: he brought up my past mistakes again yesterday)
bad.why: It is already verb plus object and takes no further object; say gen wo fan jiuzhang or fan wo de jiuzhang.

mean: a person who always makes others laugh and cheer up
lit: the pistachio, literally 'happy-heart nut': the word for the nut also names a cheerful person

use.how: A noun, usually 是……的开心果 or 一个开心果. Said warmly of a person (sometimes a pet or child) who keeps a group in good spirits.

near.diff: 活宝 is a funny, often silly character, sometimes said with mild teasing; 开心果 stresses that they lift everyone's mood.

cue: Every office has one person who tells jokes, remembers birthdays and lightens the mood when things get tense. What do you call her?

ctx.s: 她是我们班的{开心果}，大家都喜欢她。
ctx.en: She's the one who keeps our class cheerful; everyone likes her.

ctx.s: 有他在，聚会从来不冷场，他简直是个{开心果}。
ctx.en: When he's around, a party never goes flat; he's a real ray of sunshine.

ctx.s: 自从小狗来了，它就成了我们全家的{开心果}。
ctx.en: Since the puppy arrived, it has become the joy of the whole family.

ctx.s: 爷爷住院时，小孙女天天去讲笑话，成了病房里的{开心果}。
ctx.en: While Grandpa was in hospital, his little granddaughter went every day to tell jokes and cheered up the whole ward.

ctx.s: 你们部门谁是{开心果}？年会想请他来当主持人。
ctx.en: Who's the joker in your department? We'd like them to host the annual party.

ctx.s: 他平时是大家的{开心果}，没想到自己心里也有这么多烦恼。
ctx.en: He's usually the one who cheers everyone up; who'd have thought he had so many worries of his own?

bad.s: 今天考试通过了，我是{开心果}！
bad.en: (meant: I passed my exam today and I'm so happy)
bad.why: It names someone who cheers other people up, not your own happiness; just say wo hen kaixin.

bad.s: 他很{开心果}，总是笑嘻嘻的。
bad.en: (meant: he's very cheerful and always smiling)
bad.why: It is a noun and cannot follow hen like an adjective; say ta shi ge kaixinguo, or ta hen kailang (cheerful).

mean: to join in where there is fun or a crowd
lit: to draw close to where it is hot and noisy

use.how: Verb phrase: 去凑热闹, 凑个热闹, 凑凑热闹. Said of joining a lively scene for fun; 别来凑热闹 can also mean 'don't butt in and add to the trouble'.

cue: You know nothing about football, but the whole town is watching the final in the square, so you go along for the atmosphere. What are you doing?

ctx.s: 广场上在放烟花，我们也去{凑热闹}吧！
ctx.en: They're setting off fireworks in the square; let's go and join the fun!

ctx.s: 我不太懂足球，就是跟朋友去{凑个热闹}。
ctx.en: I don't really understand football; I just went along with my friends for the atmosphere.

ctx.s: 新店开张排了长队，很多人其实只是来{凑热闹}的。
ctx.en: There was a long queue when the new shop opened; a lot of people only came because of the crowd.

ctx.s: “你也报名跑马拉松了？”“我肯定跑不完，就是{凑凑热闹}。”
ctx.en: "You've signed up for the marathon too?" "I'll never finish it; I'm just joining in for fun."

ctx.s: 我这边已经忙不过来了，你就别来{凑热闹}了。
ctx.en: I'm already swamped here; please don't come and add to the chaos.

ctx.s: 庙会那天，全村老少都出来{凑热闹}，街上挤得水泄不通。
ctx.en: On the day of the temple fair, the whole village, young and old, came out to join the fun, and the streets were packed.

bad.s: 这个城市晚上很{凑热闹}。
bad.en: (meant: this city is very lively at night)
bad.why: It is a verb phrase for going to join the fun, not an adjective for a lively place; say hen renao.

bad.s: 听说邻居家着火了，我们赶紧跑去{凑热闹}，帮忙灭火。
bad.en: (meant: we heard the neighbours' house was on fire and rushed over to help put it out)
bad.why: It means going along for the fun or the spectacle; said of a fire it sounds like gawking, not helping. Say qu bangmang.

mean: to take a setback too hard and be unable to let it go
lit: to think and not be able to open up: the mind stays shut around the hurt

use.how: Potential complement used as predicate, often in 别想不开 or 一直想不开; opposite 想得开. Said with concern; 一时想不开 can hint at fear of self-harm, so it is not a light word.

near.diff: 钻牛角尖 is stubbornly fixing on a narrow or pointless question; 想不开 is being unable to get over an emotional blow.

cue: Your friend failed one job interview and has been miserable for a week, saying it proves she's useless. What do you tell her not to do?

ctx.s: 不就是一次考试没考好吗？哭一场就过去了，别{想不开}。
ctx.en: It's only one exam that went badly; have a good cry and move on, don't take it so hard.

ctx.s: 他被女朋友甩了以后一直{想不开}，天天喝闷酒。
ctx.en: Ever since his girlfriend dumped him he hasn't been able to get over it, and he drinks alone every day.

ctx.s: 被老板说了两句就难过了好几天，你怎么就{想不开}呢？
ctx.en: The boss criticised you a little and you've been upset for days; why can't you let it go?

ctx.s: 妈妈退休以后总觉得自己没用了，有点{想不开}。
ctx.en: Since retiring, Mum keeps feeling she's useless and is taking it rather hard.

ctx.s: “比赛输了，他把自己关在房间里。”“你去陪陪他，别让他{想不开}。”
ctx.en: "He lost the match and has shut himself in his room." "Go and keep him company; don't let him brood over it."

ctx.s: 遇到挫折总是{想不开}，最后苦的只是自己。
ctx.en: If you always take setbacks so hard, in the end the only one who suffers is you.

bad.s: 这道数学题太难了，我{想不开}。
bad.en: (meant: this maths problem is too hard, I can't work it out)
bad.why: It means being unable to get over something upsetting, not failing to solve a problem; say wo xiang bu chulai.

bad.s: 我一直{想不开}，他为什么突然辞职了。
bad.en: (meant: I still can't understand why he suddenly quit)
bad.why: Being puzzled is xiang bu tong; this phrase is about your own grief or resentment, not about understanding someone else.

mean: an obstacle that stands in the way of progress
lit: a stone that trips your feet

use.how: A noun, usually in 是/成为……的绊脚石. Said of a habit, problem or person that blocks progress; contrasts with 垫脚石, a stepping stone.

near.diff: 拖后腿 is a verb: someone holds a person or team back; 绊脚石 is a noun naming the obstacle itself.

cue: A good student keeps losing marks through careless mistakes, and the teacher wants to name that one habit as what's blocking her. What does the teacher call it?

ctx.s: 粗心是你学习上最大的{绊脚石}。
ctx.en: Carelessness is the biggest obstacle in your studies.

ctx.s: 骄傲往往会成为进步的{绊脚石}。
ctx.en: Arrogance often becomes a stumbling block to progress.

ctx.s: 对很多外国人来说，声调是学中文的第一块{绊脚石}。
ctx.en: For many foreigners, tones are the first stumbling block in learning Chinese.

ctx.s: 你觉得公司发展最大的{绊脚石}是什么？
ctx.en: What do you think is the biggest obstacle to the company's growth?

ctx.s: 他一直觉得，父母的反对是自己追求梦想路上的{绊脚石}。
ctx.en: He always felt his parents' opposition was what stood in the way of his dream.

ctx.s: 别让一次失败成为你前进的{绊脚石}，要把它变成垫脚石。
ctx.en: Don't let one failure become a stumbling block; turn it into a stepping stone.

bad.s: 他{绊脚石}了我的计划。
bad.en: (meant: he got in the way of my plan)
bad.why: It is a noun, not a verb; say ta cheng le wo jihua de banjiaoshi, or ta zu'ai le wo de jihua.

bad.s: 老师是我成功的{绊脚石}，帮了我很多。
bad.en: (meant: my teacher helped me a lot on my way to success)
bad.why: It means an obstacle, the opposite of help; for someone who helped you on your way say yinluren or guiren.

mean: to force someone to do what they are not able to do
lit: to drive ducks up onto a perch: ducks cannot climb up and roost the way chickens do

use.how: Predicate, often 是/被赶鸭子上架 or 这不是赶鸭子上架吗. Often said wryly of oneself when pushed into a task beyond one's skill, or as a complaint on someone's behalf.

near.diff: 强人所难 is any unreasonable demand, more formal; 赶鸭子上架 stresses that the person simply lacks the skill, and is often self-mocking.

cue: You have never spoken in public, but the host fell ill and you were pushed onto the stage to run the company party. How do you describe your situation?

ctx.s: 我从来没主持过晚会，这次完全是{赶鸭子上架}。
ctx.en: I'd never hosted a show before; I was completely thrown in at the deep end.

ctx.s: 老板让我这个新人去谈合同，真是{赶鸭子上架}。
ctx.en: The boss sent me, a newcomer, to negotiate the contract; talk about being pushed into something beyond me.

ctx.s: “你唱得不错啊，以前学过？”“哪儿啊，今天是被{赶鸭子上架}的。”
ctx.en: "You sang well! Have you had lessons?" "Not at all, I was dragged up there against my will today."

ctx.s: 孩子五音不全，你非让他去参加唱歌比赛，这不是{赶鸭子上架}吗？
ctx.en: The child can't carry a tune, yet you insist he enter a singing contest; isn't that forcing him into something he can't do?

ctx.s: 学校缺数学老师，就让体育老师顶上，这不是{赶鸭子上架}嘛。
ctx.en: The school is short of maths teachers, so they had the PE teacher fill in; that's asking him to do something he's not cut out for.

ctx.s: 妻子出差那几天，从不下厨的他只好被{赶鸭子上架}，天天给孩子做饭。
ctx.en: While his wife was away on business, he, who never cooks, had no choice but to struggle through making the kids' meals every day.

bad.s: 我快迟到了，只好{赶鸭子上架}，一路跑到车站。
bad.en: (meant: I was nearly late, so I rushed all the way to the station)
bad.why: Here gan means to drive or herd, not to hurry; the phrase is about being forced into a task beyond one's ability.

bad.s: 他是专业厨师，让他做菜真是{赶鸭子上架}。
bad.en: (meant: he is a professional chef, so asking him to cook is a natural fit)
bad.why: It only fits when the person lacks the ability; for a chef cooking, it is the opposite of the meaning.

mean: to warn someone in advance so they are prepared
lit: to give a vaccination: an injection that protects you before the illness arrives

use.how: Verb-object, in 给某人打（个）预防针; can split (打了个预防针). Said of preparing someone mentally for bad news or a disappointment before it comes.

near.diff: 打招呼 can mean giving a quiet heads-up or asking for a favour; 打预防针 is preparing someone for something unwelcome.

cue: Before the exam results come out, a teacher tells her class the paper was marked very strictly this year, so they won't be shocked. What is she doing?

ctx.s: 我先给你{打个预防针}：这次考试特别难。
ctx.en: Let me warn you in advance: this exam is especially hard.

ctx.s: 项目可能会延期，我得提前给客户{打打预防针}。
ctx.en: The project may be delayed, so I need to prepare the client for it ahead of time.

ctx.s: 面试前，师兄给我{打了预防针}：那位面试官说话非常直接。
ctx.en: Before the interview, a senior student warned me that the interviewer is very blunt.

ctx.s: 涨价的事，你跟顾客{打过预防针}没有？
ctx.en: Have you given customers advance warning about the price rise?

ctx.s: 搬家前，妈妈就给孩子{打了预防针}，说刚到新学校可能会有点孤单。
ctx.en: Before the move, Mum prepared the child, saying it might be a bit lonely at first at the new school.

ctx.s: 经理开会时早就{打过预防针}，所以名单公布后，大家并不太意外。
ctx.en: The manager had warned everyone at the meeting, so when the list came out, nobody was very surprised.

bad.s: 会议结束后，他才给我们{打预防针}，说方案已经被否了。
bad.en: (meant: after the meeting he told us the plan had been rejected)
bad.why: It is a warning given before the bad news lands; telling people afterwards is simply informing them (gaosu).

bad.s: 我昨天{打预防针}他了。
bad.en: (meant: I warned him in advance yesterday)
bad.why: It is verb plus object and cannot take a person as object; say wo zuotian gei ta da le yufangzhen.

mean: to hold back some of one's skill or plans just in case
lit: to keep one move back: not show your whole hand

use.how: Verb phrase, often 留了一手 or 总爱留一手. Said of teachers or rivals not showing all they know (a complaint), or of keeping a fallback (prudence).

near.diff: 卖关子 is deliberately keeping listeners in suspense at the key point of a story; 留一手 is keeping back skill or resources for oneself.

cue: Your aunt taught you her famous dumpling recipe, but yours never taste the same and you suspect she left out one secret step. What do you accuse her of?

ctx.s: 你教我做菜是不是{留了一手}？我做的怎么没你的好吃？
ctx.en: Did you hold something back when you taught me that dish? Why doesn't mine taste as good as yours?

ctx.s: 跟他谈判要小心，这个人做事总爱{留一手}。
ctx.en: Be careful negotiating with him; he always keeps something up his sleeve.

ctx.s: 做生意得{留一手}，不能把所有的钱都投进去。
ctx.en: In business you have to keep something in reserve; you can't put all your money in.

ctx.s: “你怎么把最好的方案留到最后才拿出来？”“谈判嘛，总得{留一手}。”
ctx.en: "Why did you only bring out your best proposal at the very end?" "It's a negotiation; you always keep something in reserve."

ctx.s: 以前有的老师傅教徒弟时{留一手}，怕徒弟以后超过自己。
ctx.en: In the past some old craftsmen held back part of their skill from apprentices, afraid of being surpassed.

ctx.s: 原来他前几轮都{留了一手}，到决赛才拿出真本事。
ctx.en: It turned out he'd been holding back in the early rounds and only showed what he could really do in the final.

bad.s: 他对我很好，吃饭时总给我{留一手}。
bad.en: (meant: he's good to me and always saves me some food)
bad.why: It is about holding back skill or keeping a fallback, not saving food for someone; say gei wo liu yi fen.

bad.s: 这个箱子太重了，你能{留一手}帮我抬一下吗？
bad.en: (meant: this box is too heavy, can you lend me a hand?)
bad.why: Liu means to keep back, the opposite of helping; to lend a hand is da ba shou or bang ge mang.

mean: to turn the clock back and reverse progress
lit: to drive the car in reverse

use.how: Predicate, often 是在开倒车 or the set phrase 开历史的倒车. Criticises a policy, rule or practice that deliberately goes back to an older, worse way.

near.diff: 走下坡路 is a gradual decline that just happens; 开倒车 is a deliberate step backwards that someone chooses.

cue: A company that switched to online forms years ago suddenly orders everyone back to paper forms signed in triplicate. What do the staff say management is doing?

ctx.s: 现在还要用纸质表格登记，简直是在{开倒车}。
ctx.en: Still making people register on paper forms these days is really turning the clock back.

ctx.s: 这项新规定取消了员工的带薪假，被很多人批评是{开倒车}。
ctx.en: The new rule abolished staff paid leave, and many criticised it as a step backwards.

ctx.s: 别的学校都在减轻学生负担，我们反而增加考试，这不是{开倒车}吗？
ctx.en: Other schools are lightening students' workload while we're adding more exams; isn't that going backwards?

ctx.s: “新经理把以前的审批流程又恢复了。”“唉，又在{开倒车}。”
ctx.en: "The new manager has brought back the old approval process." "Sigh, turning the clock back again."

ctx.s: 这个城市拆掉了自行车道，重新扩建停车场，有人说这是在{开倒车}。
ctx.en: The city tore up its cycle lanes to build more car parks, and some say that's reversing progress.

ctx.s: 在环保问题上{开历史的倒车}，只会让后代付出代价。
ctx.en: Turning back the clock on environmental protection will only make future generations pay.

bad.s: 爷爷最近身体越来越差，健康在{开倒车}。
bad.en: (meant: Grandpa's health has been getting worse lately)
bad.why: It criticises a chosen step backwards in policy or practice; for health gradually declining use zou xiapo lu.

bad.s: 我们{开倒车}一下，再讨论一遍第一个问题吧。
bad.en: (meant: let's go back and discuss the first point again)
bad.why: It is a criticism of reversing progress, not a neutral 'go back'; say huidao di yi ge wenti.

mean: to go downhill and steadily decline

use.how: Predicate, often 开始走下坡路, 一直在走下坡路 or 走上了下坡路. Said of health, business, careers, grades or teams declining over time.

near.diff: 开倒车 accuses someone of deliberately reversing progress; 走下坡路 simply describes a gradual decline.

cue: A once-popular restaurant has had fewer customers every year since its famous chef left. How would you describe its business?

ctx.s: 爷爷年纪大了，身体开始{走下坡路}了。
ctx.en: Grandpa is getting old, and his health has started to go downhill.

ctx.s: 这家老字号自从换了老板，生意就一直在{走下坡路}。
ctx.en: Ever since this old shop changed hands, its business has been going steadily downhill.

ctx.s: 你最近成绩怎么{走下坡路}了？是不是游戏玩得太多了？
ctx.en: Why have your grades been slipping lately? Have you been playing too many games?

ctx.s: 球队连输了好几场，球迷都担心球队要{走下坡路}了。
ctx.en: The team has lost several games in a row, and the fans are worried it's starting to decline.

ctx.s: “那个牌子以前很火啊。”“早就{走下坡路}了，现在没什么人买。”
ctx.en: "That brand used to be really popular." "It's been in decline for ages; hardly anyone buys it now."

ctx.s: 随着网购兴起，许多实体书店都{走上了下坡路}。
ctx.en: With the rise of online shopping, many bricks-and-mortar bookshops have gone into decline.

bad.s: 他的病{走下坡路}了，很快就能出院。
bad.en: (meant: his illness is easing and he'll soon leave hospital)
bad.why: Going downhill means getting worse, not the illness going away; for recovery say bingqing haozhuan le.

bad.s: 新校长故意{走下坡路}，把以前的改革全取消了。
bad.en: (meant: the new head deliberately undid all the earlier reforms)
bad.why: It describes a decline that happens over time, not a deliberate choice; for undoing progress use kai daoche.
